classification.difficultyReason: Identify all three orders for exactly one dark chocolate, track the remaining counts on each path, and combine the disjoint path probabilities.

content.prompt: A box contains twelve identical looking chocolates. However, four are milk chocolate and eight are dark chocolate. Nathan eats three chocolates chosen randomly from the box. Using a tree diagram, or otherwise, find the probability that

children.label: a
children.prompt: the first chocolate eaten is a dark chocolate.

answer.worked:
After each dark chocolate is eaten, one fewer dark chocolate and one fewer chocolate in total remain.

$$\begin{align*} P(\text{three dark}) &= \frac{8}{12}\times\frac{7}{11}\times\frac{6}{10} \\ P(\text{three dark}) &= \frac{14}{55} \end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Nathan eats exactly one dark chocolate.

answer.worked:
Let $D$ stand for dark and $M$ for milk. The paths $DMM$, $MDM$ and $MMD$ use the same factors in different orders.

$$\begin{align*} P(\text{one dark}) &= P(DMM)+P(MDM)+P(MMD) \\ P(\text{one dark}) &= 3\times\frac{8}{12}\times\frac{4}{11}\times\frac{3}{10} \\ P(\text{one dark}) &= \frac{12}{55} \end{align*}$$
